summary: Redwood team gave a Console-focused walkthrough for Brightline covering per-route usage analytics, cost breakdowns, and recommended Optimize settings. Brightline is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a pilot; security/compliance and predictable unit cost are primary concerns. Agreed next steps: share pricing/TCO, demo recording, and Brightline will provide traces for a tailored cost projection.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-18 16:00 PST | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Jordan Miller, Priya Kapoor, Liam O'Connor, Maya Tan - Redwood; Alicia Gomez, Mark Liu, Sofia Alvarez, Devon Park - Brightline

[00:00] Jordan Miller: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - I'm Jordan, AE on the account. Priya our SE will run through the Console demo.
[00:10] Alicia Gomez: Hi, Alicia here - Head of AI at Brightline. We invited Mark and Sofia cause they'll own the platform and security review.
[00:15] Priya Kapoor: Great, thanks. we'll jump in. agenda: per-route dashboards, usage analytics, cost breakdowns, and a brief look at Optimize recommendations. we'll leave time for Qs.
[00:30] Mark Liu: For context, our current stack is a mix of hosted LLM endpoints and some self-hosted smaller models. we're trying to understand the unit economics and how Redwood would slot in.
[00:40] Priya Kapoor: Totally. first screen - the usage overview. this shows tokens in vs tokens out, requests per second, and route-level latency percentiles. you can filter by model, route, or time window.
[01:05] Priya Kapoor: (click) here you can see per-route breakdowns. e.g., /generate-inbox and /summarize-docs. each route has cost, latency, token counts, and error rates. you can export CSV for accounting.
[01:25] Jordan Miller: One thing customers like is the token-level cost line item - it shows prompt vs completion tokens and how much you're charged. that helps you spot chatty prompts.
[01:40] Devon Park: Is that cost computed from our current pricing or Redwood's estimate?
[01:45] Jordan Miller: good call. the Console shows estimated cost using your pricing profile we configure. during a pilot we can map it to hosted rates or dedicated reserved capacity assumptions.
[02:05] Mark Liu: We'd want to compare hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved monthly commit. can the console model both?
[02:12] Priya Kapoor: yes - you can toggle pricing scenarios. we have templates: hosted usage, dedicated committed, and mixed. the cost breakdown view also attributes cost to routes so product owners can see which features are driving spend.
[02:40] [02:40] Sofia Alvarez: we need to confirm data residency and KMS integration - will logs or tokens be accessible to anyone at Redwood?
[02:50] Jordan Miller: short answer: for Dedicated or Private, customer data stays in their VPC; for Hosted we store minimal retention per your policy and we have SOC2 and ISO documents. we can integrate with your KMS for key control.
[03:10] Priya Kapoor: (narration) back to dashboards - here's a cost drilldown. you can group by model variant, quantization profile, or route. e.g., if /summarize-docs is using a 2x larger context model, you see cost spike and latency bump.
[03:35] Mark Liu: that per-route view would be huge for us. product folks can tie features to dollars. how granular are the latency percentiles? 50/90/99?
[03:45] Priya Kapoor: 50/90/99 and p999 for some routes if you enable extended tracing. there's also tail latency histograms.
[04:05] Jordan Miller: another feature - you can set alerts for cost thresholds per route and get recommended Optimize changes, like batching or enabling prefix caching for a route.
[04:20] Alicia Gomez: how does recommended batching affect latency? our SLA for some routes is sub-200ms.
[04:28] Priya Kapoor: batching is workload-dependent. Optimize will recommend per-route batching that aims to keep latency within your SLO. for strict low-latency routes we recommend no batching or tiny batches and instead use dedicated capacity or KV caching.
[04:50] Mark Liu: what's KV cache again in your infra? is it like a prefix cache?
[04:55] Priya Kapoor: yeah, K-V cache - it's prefix caching of hidden states so repeat context doesn't recompute. great for short-context reuse like chat or re-used prompts. can reduce cost significantly.
[05:10] [05:10] Liam O'Connor: (interject) and our runtime chooses kernels and quantization automatically based on model and hardware - that's why the Console shows a recommended quantization profile per route.
[05:30] Sofia Alvarez: security question - audit logs. can we get token-level audit logs and SAML SSO?
[05:36] Jordan Miller: yes we support SSO / SAML and RBAC. audit logs are available; we can stream them to your SIEM. for hosted we keep logs with configurable retention and for Private we hand full control to your infra.
[05:55] Mark Liu: any third-party integrations - Datadog, Snowflake, BigQuery?
[06:00] Priya Kapoor: we have exporters and webhooks. CSV export is simplest for finance. we can push usage to BigQuery via our connector.
[06:18] Alicia Gomez: I saw Optimize recommendations earlier - show an example?
[06:22] Priya Kapoor: sure - here a route had 70% identical prefixes. Optimize suggested prefix caching + move to a quantized 4-bit profile and estimated 3x cost reduction with a small 5% latency increase on p99.
[06:45] Devon Park: do you have concrete TCO math? like per-100M tokens hosted vs dedicated?
[06:50] Jordan Miller: we'll send a tailored pricing deck but as an example, hosted might be cheaper at small scale; dedicated wins after sustained throughput because of reserved GPU efficiency. we'll model this for your traces.
[07:10] [07:10] Priya Kapoor: can we ask for a sample of your traces - one week of routes and payload sizes? that lets us run the Console's cost projection tool against realistic traffic.
[07:20] Mark Liu: yes, we can pull anonymized traces. no payload content, just sizes and route ids.
[07:28] Sofia Alvarez: we will need to review your SOC2 and encryption docs before a pilot.
[07:34] Jordan Miller: absolutely - i'll include our security pack; Priya will attach the architecture diagram for Dedicated and Private.
[07:47] Priya Kapoor: quick note on fallbacks - Console lets you configure routing policies. if Dedicated is saturated, you can fallback to hosted variant to keep app online.
[08:00] Alicia Gomez: ok that addresses reliability concerns. any limitations on model variants we should know?
[08:07] Priya Kapoor: current catalog supports common open models and some Redwood-verified variants; custom model imports are supported in Private deployments. we'll discuss model onboarding in the pilot scoping.
[08:25] Mark Liu: our biggest worry is unexpected spend - can we set hard caps per route?
[08:30] Jordan Miller: yes, rate limits and budget alerts. and Console supports per-route spending caps and automatic route throttles or fallbacks.
[08:45] Devon Park: can we see an example CSV export?
[08:48] Priya Kapoor: i'll share one after the call. it includes route, timestamp, tokens, cost-attribution, latency metrics.
[09:00] [09:00] Jordan Miller: quick Q - competitors. any existing vendor you're evaluating?
[09:05] Alicia Gomez: mainly Anthropic and Vertex AI for managed endpoints. cost and compliance are big factors.
[09:12] Jordan Miller: noted. we have benchmark writeups - i'll include relevant ones.
[09:20] Priya Kapoor: wrapping up demo - key takeaways: Console surfaces per-route cost, recommends Optimize actions, supports pricing scenario modeling, and integrates with security controls.
[09:35] Sofia Alvarez: can you highlight default retention for logs and token data on hosted?
[09:40] Jordan Miller: default is 30 days for hosted usage logs; audit logs are 90 days but we can extend for a fee. for Private, retention is customer-controlled.
[09:55] Mark Liu: timeline - we want to run a 4-6 week pilot early next year.
[10:00] Jordan Miller: that fits. next steps recap: jordan sends pricing + SLA + security pack; priya shares demo recording + CSV sample; brightline to provide traces; schedule pilot scoping.
[10:20] Alicia Gomez: thanks, that was helpful. we'll review and aim to get traces this week.
[10:30] Jordan Miller: great, thanks everyone. end call.

[End of transcript]
